stories.body: US and Iranian officials held their first talks since June on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, using Qatari mediators who shuttled between the delegations. US envoy Steve Witkoff called the discussions constructive and promising, while President Donald Trump described them as productive and said further talks were expected. Iran said any progress depended on ending US military and economic pressure, including blockades and sanctions; a senior Iranian official indicated Tehran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if Washington took reciprocal steps. The contact came as Trump publicly threatened to “annihilate” Iran if no settlement is reached and as the war's disruption of the strait continues to affect global energy markets.
stories.headline: US and Iran hold mediated talks at the UN amid escalating rhetoric

stories.body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Kyiv is prepared to stop strikes on Russian energy facilities if Moscow stops attacking Ukraine's power, heating and water systems. Speaking after talks with US President Donald Trump and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham in New York, Zelenskyy said an energy ceasefire could provide a route toward diplomacy before winter, but rejected any unilateral halt to attacks on Russia's oil industry. He also warned that intelligence indicated Russia was preparing a new large-scale attack, and argued that sanctions relief could not be considered while Ukraine remains under missile and drone threat.
stories.headline: Zelenskyy says Ukraine is ready for an energy ceasefire with Russia

stories.body: The United States, Denmark and Greenland signed an updated defence agreement allowing Washington to establish additional defence areas at Narsarsuaq in southern Greenland and Mestersvig in the east, while modernising activities at Pituffik Space Base. The pact explicitly reaffirms Danish sovereignty, Greenlandic self-determination and the need for Danish and Greenlandic approval of technical arrangements, ending a period of tension prompted by Trump's earlier calls to acquire the territory. It also bars non-NATO countries from establishing military installations or a persistent military presence on the island. The agreement still requires approval by the Danish and Greenlandic parliaments.
stories.headline: US, Denmark and Greenland agree to expand American military presence

stories.body: The European Union agreed to remove Russian billionaires Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list while extending restrictions on nearly 3,000 people and companies linked to Russia's war in Ukraine for three years. The decision followed difficult unanimous negotiations: France sought Usmanov's removal on reported national-security grounds, while Luxembourg supported delisting Fridman amid his legal challenge over frozen assets. Ukraine condemned the move as unacceptable and warned that it signals division and impunity, while Ireland, holding the EU presidency, described the package as a difficult compromise that makes the broader sanctions framework more durable.
stories.headline: EU removes Usmanov and Fridman from Russia sanctions list

stories.body: Hurricane Polo strengthened from a tropical storm into a Category 5 hurricane in less than 24 hours off Mexico's southwest coast, with sustained winds reported between 165 and 180 mph. Forecasters say the storm is being fuelled by exceptionally warm Pacific waters associated with a record-strength El Niño and could remain extremely powerful for several days. Polo is not expected to make a direct landfall, but Mexico's Pacific coast faces heavy rain, possible flooding and mudslides, dangerous surf and rip currents, particularly in Jalisco, Colima and Michoacán.
stories.headline: Hurricane Polo rapidly intensifies into Category 5 storm off Mexico

stories.body: A Washington Post investigation says the ICE officer involved in the shooting of Wilber Garcés Pérez in Texas was a recent recruit hired during the agency's expansion and was not using a body camera. Pérez says that after being shot he was moved from hospital into ICE detention within hours, despite a bullet remaining near his spine, and was forced to sleep on the floor. The case has intensified scrutiny of how ICE recruits have been vetted and trained, as well as the agency's use of body cameras during enforcement operations.
stories.headline: Texas ICE shooting raises questions over recruitment and body-camera practices

stories.body: Several Republican Senate candidates in competitive races are distancing themselves from President Donald Trump over the Iran war as high fuel prices become a major electoral concern. Ohio Senator Jon Husted said the conflict needs to end as quickly as possible, joining Iowa candidate Ashley Hinson and Michigan candidate Mike Rogers in calling for a faster resolution. Candidates have linked the war and rising diesel prices to pressure on households, farmers and truckers, while some Republicans are also proposing measures such as a temporary diesel export ban or state gas-tax relief. Trump said his administration was considering an export ban, though the idea faces opposition from oil-state Republicans.
stories.headline: Republican Senate candidates call for a quick end to the Iran war

stories.body: Senator Roger Wicker, the Republican chair of the Senate Armed Services Committee, criticized the planned meeting between President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. Wicker said he opposed the “lavish welcome” being prepared for Xi, whom he described as an oppressive dictator, highlighting unease among some congressional Republicans over the administration's approach to China.
stories.headline: Senate Armed Services chair criticizes planned Trump-Xi meeting

stories.body: The US Supreme Court declined an emergency appeal from surrogate McKenna West, leaving in place a California ruling that grants custody of a newborn to the couple who hired her. West refused the parents' request to terminate the pregnancy after a 20-week scan found that the fetus had a severe heart defect, travelled to Texas, and gave birth there. She argued that the biological parents might not pursue necessary treatment because they had sought an abortion; the parents say West withheld medical information and maintain that the child is theirs. The baby, who has hypoplastic left heart syndrome, remains seriously ill and requires complex medical care.
stories.headline: Supreme Court declines to intervene in surrogate custody dispute

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said Spain has asked Morocco for urgent action and explanations after the failure of border controls that preceded the mass entry of more than 80,000 migrants into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July. In an interview in New York, Sánchez said Spain needed a constructive relationship with Rabat but that Morocco's control mechanism had clearly failed. Spain is preparing to send Morocco files concerning migrant minors in Ceuta to explore family reunification, although officials acknowledge that earlier requests have often received no response and that the process may take months.
stories.headline: Spain presses Morocco for answers over Ceuta border-control failure

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court has taken a step toward extending the amnesty for embezzlement to leaders of the Catalan independence movement, potentially clearing the way for the Supreme Court to lift the arrest warrant against former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont. The court is expected to rule on 6 October on appeals involving former ministers Jordi Turull and Dolors Bassa. If it upholds the amnesty in those cases and its reasoning applies more broadly, investigating judge Pablo Llarena is expected to lift Puigdemont's warrant without waiting for the Constitutional Court to decide Puigdemont's own appeal.
stories.headline: Constitutional Court ruling brings Puigdemont closer to lifting of arrest warrant

stories.body: The OECD raised its forecast for Spanish economic growth in 2026 by four tenths of a percentage point to 2.6%, putting Spain ahead of most major eurozone economies and broadly in line with the government's forecast. The organisation cited strong domestic demand and a solid second quarter, while projecting growth of 1.8% in 2027. It also warned that inflation will remain a major concern, revising its 2026 forecast to 3.7% and its 2027 forecast to 3.4%, with higher international energy prices likely to keep Spanish inflation above the European average.
stories.headline: OECD raises Spain's 2026 growth forecast to 2.6% but warns on inflation

stories.body: Barcelona's Fabra i Puig Rodalies station remains closed after part of a false ceiling collapsed in the concourse on Tuesday afternoon, lightly injuring three people who were taken to Vall d'Hebron Hospital. R4 trains are continuing to run but are not stopping at the station, and passengers are being directed to use La Sagrera-Meridiana and Metro line 1. The closure adds to a difficult day for the Rodalies network, with delays and infrastructure incidents affecting several lines, including a reported cable theft between Badalona and El Clot.
stories.headline: Fabra i Puig commuter-rail station remains closed after ceiling collapse

stories.body: Catalan president Salvador Illa acknowledged that the administration made serious and unacceptable errors in administering the 2025 PISA tests, leaving the results unrepresentative. More than 23% of selected students were exempted, far above the OECD's recommended maximum of 5%, largely among pupils with learning, behavioural, emotional or language-support needs. Illa said warnings from the national education-evaluation institute during the testing period did not reach schools or political leaders in the Education Department. The government has replaced the department's senior civil servant and opened disciplinary proceedings against three people, while opposition parties have demanded further political accountability.
stories.headline: Illa admits serious failures in Catalonia's PISA assessment process

stories.body: Barcelona bus workers have voted to call further partial strikes unless they reach an agreement with Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona within the next two weeks on a collective agreement that has been stalled since late 2025. The workers want a 35-hour week, more consistent rest periods and additional hiring to reduce workload and improve work-life balance. The decision followed a seven-hour strike on Tuesday, when minimum service levels were set at 20% for most of the day and 40% during the afternoon peak. The union says more stoppages could follow in October or November if TMB does not make an acceptable proposal.
stories.headline: Barcelona bus workers threaten further strikes without a deal with TMB

stories.body: Barcelona's La Mercè festival begins on 23 September with five days of free outdoor programming across all ten districts, including 109 concerts, 55 popular-culture performances and 180 street-arts shows. New and expanded venues include Plaça de les Glòries, Park Güell, Fort Pienc and the Bogatell beach area, where the festival's piromusical will be staged. Highlights include a large-format performance by La Fura dels Baus at Moll de la Fusta, the Correfoc along Passeig de Gràcia, and concerts by artists including Love of Lesbian, La Pegatina, Els Amics de les Arts and Nacho Vegas.
stories.headline: Barcelona launches La Mercè with expanded venues and a beachside piromusical
